tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
The **faces** of a polyhedron are the polygonal sides that construct it. 

Let's consider the triangular prism below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14240559/assets/4e0550f18e27ad9326b5606f23b502ff6879d2149f5bac5e2fcc829506748f0b.png)

Our triangular prism has $5$ faces:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14240559/assets/cabe6f9d976ad0b577d8a12b22fda051a284416c284b88c90723bbbcbcd0f723.png)

The **vertices** of a polyhedron are its corners. Our triangular prism has $6$ vertices:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14240559/assets/153dffffba0e8e344f667d9b4aa0badbd8b6560bdf731b75b1a3efafd2c2a7cc.png)

The **edges** of a polyhedron are the straight line segments that connect its vertices. Our triangular prism has $9$ edges:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14240559/assets/b001673f783be6e9cb45fe42375d460fbe5aa760843b02ad480b340641b5c3bc.png)
